name: Bluebell
family: Asparagaceae, the asparagus family (the hyacinth group)
grown_as: The native English bluebell, grown wild in William's orchard from seed.
habit: Clumps of floppy, glossy strap leaves 20 to 45 cm long lying out from the bulb, with a flower stem 20 to 50 cm tall that droops over at the top. Forms carpets in woods.

leaf.arrangement: Three to six leaves from the base of each bulb, arching over and lying out
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, 20 to 45 cm by 7 to 15 mm, even width, narrowing only at the tip
leaf.base: Pale where it leaves the soil
leaf.surface: Glossy, smooth and fleshy, channelled along the middle

flower.form: Narrow hanging bells along one side of a stem that arches over at the tip
flower.petals: Six tepals, joined only at the base into a narrow tube, their tips curled back
flower.centre: Creamy white anthers just inside the mouth
flower.behind: A pair of narrow bluish bracts at the base of each short flower stalk
flower.carried: Five to fifteen flowers hanging down one side of the stem, which bends over at the top so the spike droops
flower.size: Each bell 1.5 to 2 cm long and narrow

fruit: Oval three-sided green capsules about 1.5 cm, held upright on their stalks along the stem, which straightens. They ripen straw-coloured and split into three to release black seeds. The dry stem stands into summer.
seedling: Not drawn. A single grass-like leaf; about five years to flower.
winter: Leaf tips come up from January; nothing above ground in late summer and autumn.

leaf: a long narrow strap leaf, even width
bloom: a narrow tubular bell with six tepal tips curled back
bulb: a white, rounded bulb about 2 to 3 cm with no papery brown skin
shoots: glossy strap leaves coming up in a bunch
the flower spike rising with its tip hooked over
flower: bells hanging along one side of the stem only
the top of the stem drooping over
long glossy leaves lying out round the base
seedhead: oval pods held upright along a straightened stem
dormant: the white bulb deep below ground

look_alikes: Spanish bluebell (Hyacinthoides hispanica) and the common hybrid have upright stems with flowers all round, wider open bells with spreading tips, blue anthers, broader leaves (to 3.5 cm) and no scent. Grape hyacinths have tiny bead-like bells in a dense spike.
